results.author: Fazlur Rahman
highlights:
Fazlur Rahman September 23, 2026· Updated October 27, 2026 7 min read

Lambda Labs GPU pricing 2026: H100 PCIe 1x at $3.29/GPU-hr; H100 SXM 1x at $4.29/GPU-hr; H100 SXM 8x at $3.99/GPU-hr; B200 SXM 8x at $6.69/GPU-hr; A100 PCIe 40GB at $1.99/GPU-hr. Lambda 1-Click Cluster reserved pricing starts at $5.54/GPU-hr at 256-GPU scale. Lambda bills per-minute with no egress fees.

Last verified: Sep 16, 2026.

...

## On-Demand Cloud pricing breakdown

Lambda On-Demand Cloud publishes per-GPU-hour rates for 10 GPU SKUs with explicit instance configurations.

Verified July 2026 (lambda.ai/instances):

- Quadro RTX 6000 (24 GB, 14 vCPUs, 46 GiB RAM, 512 GiB SSD): $0.69/GPU-hr — legacy visualization card
- Tesla V100 (16 GB, 88 vCPUs, 448 GiB RAM, 5.8 TiB SSD): $0.79/GPU-hr
- RTX A6000 (48 GB, 14 vCPUs, 100 GiB RAM, 512 GiB SSD): $1.09/GPU-hr
- A10 (24 GB, 30 vCPUs, 226 GiB RAM, 1.3 TiB SSD): $1.29/GPU-hr
- A100 PCIe 40GB (40 GB, 30 vCPUs, 225 GiB RAM, 512 GiB SSD): $1.99/GPU-hr
- A100 SXM 80GB (80 GB, 240 vCPUs, 1.8 TB RAM, 19.5 TiB SSD): $2.79/GPU-hr on 8x
- GH200 (96 GB, 64 vCPUs, 432 GiB RAM, 4 TiB SSD): $2.29/GPU-hr
- H100 PCIe 1x (80 GB, 26 vCPUs, 225 GiB RAM, 1 TiB SSD): $3.29/GPU-hr
- H100 SXM 1x (80 GB, 26 vCPUs, 450 GiB RAM, 5.5 TiB SSD): $4.29/GPU-hr
- B200 SXM6 8x (180 GB, 208 vCPUs, 2.9 TB RAM, 22 TiB SSD): $6.69/GPU-hr
- B200 SXM6 1x (180 GB, 26 vCPUs, 360 GiB RAM, 2.75 TiB SSD): $6.99/GPU-hr

Lambda's B300-class hardware is not yet listed on the On-Demand Cloud card (the homepage mentions GB300, B300, B200, H200 infrastructure for larger deployments, but self-serve pricing is still pending). For B300 access the path is 1-Click Cluster reservation or sales engagement.

...

On-Demand Cloud instances bill by the minute in 1-minute increments, starting after launch and health checks and ending at termination. Running instances accrue charges whether or not they are actively used — so shutting down idle instances saves real money. There is no setup fee. There are no commitment minimums on On-Demand Cloud (1-Click Clusters require 2-week minimum).

Storage is metered separately and billed per GB-month for attached volumes. Snapshot fees apply for stored images. Inter-region transfer is metered by the GB. Egress to the internet is free. Lambda publishes its full billing structure on docs.lambda.ai and surfaces the line items on the dashboard — no surprise charges.

results.author: Bobby Clay, Founder, AIForge Works
highlights:
## Editor's note

Comparable public on-demand per-GPU rates were effectively flat again this week. The transaction benchmark was not.

Across the nine providers we track, no directly comparable public on-demand per-GPU rate moved more than our 1% reporting threshold. The Ornn × ICE transaction-price index (OCPI) rose across all four tracked families over the seven days through September 8: H200 increased 8.9% to $4.91 per GPU-hour, H100 SXM increased 8.8% to $3.08, B200 increased 5.0% to $6.72, and A100 SXM4 increased 2.0% to $1.02. These OCPI readings are one day newer than the September 7 catalog snapshot and are separate from the catalog-movement result.

...

These catalog observations do not prove a launch, added capacity, retirement, orderability, or current availability. Verify the exact GPU, region, purchase terms, and availability before treating any listing as a buying option.

...

results.title: Flopper Now Tracks GPU Rental Prices Across 24 Cloud Providers | Flopper.io
highlights:
Flopper.io started as a specification database: peak TFLOPS by precision, memory, bandwidth and power for every datacenter GPU. Specs answer half of the buying question. The other half is price, and that number lives on 24 different pricing pages, in 24 different units. As of today, the pricing index collects 337 live listings from 24 GPU cloud providers, covering 89 GPUs, normalized to one unit: US dollars per GPU per hour. The pipeline refreshes every six hours and has recorded every price change since 14 July 2026, so each GPU page now carries a price history alongside its spec sheet.

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NVIDIA H100 SXM5 80 GB | 16 | $1.79/hr | $12.29/hr |
| NVIDIA A100 SXM4 80 GB | 11 | $1.40/hr | $4.10/hr |
| NVIDIA L40S 48 GB | 11 | $0.87/hr | $2.25/hr |

| NVIDIA B300 SXM 288 GB | 6 | $7.40/hr | $11.19/hr |
| AMD Instinct MI300X 192 GB | 5 | $2.39/hr | $6.00/hr |

On-demand, per-GPU, USD, as recorded on 9 September 2026. Spot, community and reserved listings are excluded from the range. Each GPU links to its live pricing page, which will have moved on by the time you read this.

...

- Per GPU, per hour, in USD. Node prices are divided by the GPU count. Monthly rates are divided by 730 hours. Non-USD prices are converted at the live exchange rate on the day of the sync.
- Pricing types are kept apart. On-demand (191 listings), spot or preemptible (31), marketplace community hosts (111) and reserved commitments (4) never share a row. The headline cheapest price on each GPU page is always on-demand, so an interruptible instance cannot masquerade as the market rate.
- Every listing maps to one canonical part. A provider's "H100" is matched to the exact variant it sells, SXM5 or PCIe, 80 GB or 94 GB, so a PCIe price never dilutes the SXM figure. Names the matcher cannot place are logged and dropped rather than guessed.
- Bad data is quarantined, not published. A listing that lands far outside its GPU's price band is held back and flagged for review. Median, dispersion and FP8-per-dollar figures on the pricing index are calculated so that a single bad listing cannot move them.

results.title: What is a neocloud, and how does it price GPUs?
results.author: The Hardware Desk
highlights: Lambda prices per GPU rather than per node: its H100 SXM runs $3.99 to $4.29 per GPU-hour on-demand and its B200 SXM6 runs $6.69 to $6.99, both lower than CoreWeave’s equivalent on-demand figures, which is consistent with Lambda competing on price within the same neocloud-giant tier. Against both of those sits Ornn Data’s blended H100 index, the same number that answers how much does it cost to rent an H100 per hour?, which settled at $2.68 per GPU-hour on 2026-08-26, below every on-demand figure above because the index averages across many providers and contract structures, including the deep reserved discounts that never show up on a public on-demand rate card. CoreWeave doesn’t publish what those reserved rates actually are by term length or volume, only that committed usage saves “up to 60% over on-demand prices,” so the number a given customer pays sits somewhere between that index average and the on-demand ceiling depending entirely on what they’re willing to sign. Underneath all of this, CoreWeave reported $2.078 billion in Q1 2026 revenue and a 56% adjusted EBITDA margin against that $99.4 billion backlog, evidence that the reserved side of the business, not the on-demand sticker, is what actually funds the buildout.
